title: Piper PA-28-181 Archer III — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Piper PA-28-181 Archer III with Lycoming O-360 carbureted engine. Memory items are marked accordingly. Contains no numeric limitations; all airspeeds and power settings must come from the specific aircraft POH. The O-360 is carbureted — carburetor ice is applicable and included. Aviate first; use this checklist as an aide-memoire only.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the Piper PA-28-181 Archer III and Lycoming O-360 carbureted engine emergency procedures.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, or other numeric limits — must come from aircraft POH.
Emergency procedures must be studied, briefed, and practiced. This file is an aide-memoire. Aviate first, then navigate and communicate.
Equipment variations across this production run may affect available systems during emergencies. Verify all procedures against the specific aircraft POH before flight.

Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN — draw fuel remaining in the induction system away from the fire

items.text: Ignition
Master switch
Heater and vents — close all fresh-air vents and cabin heat to reduce airflow feeding the fire
Airspeed — increase to a speed that may help extinguish the fire by slipstream; do not exceed Vne
Forced landing — execute forced landing procedure immediately; do not delay for a restart

sections.title: Engine Fire on Ground (During or After Start)

items.text: Starter — continue cranking if fire is in the induction system; cranking may draw fire back through the intake
Throttle — advance to assist drawing fuel and fire into the engine if induction fire
Mixture
Fuel selector
Ignition
Master switch
Evacuate — exit all occupants immediately; move upwind away from the aircraft
Fire extinguisher — use only if fire is small, accessible, and escape route is clear
Master switch
Avionics master switch
All electrical switches — lights, fan, pitot heat
Vents — open to vent smoke from cockpit; fresh air assists in clearing fumes
Fire extinguisher — discharge toward source of smoke if identified and accessible
Land as soon as practicable — smoke or fumes indicate a potential for rapid fire spread; do not delay
Electrical switches — after smoke clears, restore individual switches one at a time to identify the faulty circuit before landing
Circuit breakers — do not reset a tripped breaker in flight unless essential for safety; a tripped breaker indicates a fault
Oil pressure gauge — verify indication; cross-check oil temperature for confirming trend
Throttle — reduce power to minimum needed to maintain flight; lower power reduces engine stress
Landing area — identify a suitable field or airport within close range; engine seizure may be imminent
Mayday call — declare emergency with position, nature of malfunction, and intentions
Land as soon as possible — if pressure is zero or temperature is rising abnormally, do not delay; engine seizure can occur without warning
After landing — do not run the engine; inspect for oil loss before any further operation
Carburetor heat — apply FULL ON at first sign of unexplained RPM loss or engine roughness in cruise or descent
RPM — monitor for initial further drop as ice melts and passes through the induction system, followed by recovery
Throttle — avoid large changes while carburetor heat is applied; heat reduces available power
Carburetor heat — leave ON until RPM recovers and stabilizes above original indication; then return to COLD
items.response: LEAVE ON UNTIL RECOVERED; THEN COLD

items.text: If RPM does not recover — land as soon as practicable; severe ice accumulation may not fully clear with heat alone

Icing conditions — if conditions are conducive to carburetor ice (temperature between approximately 20 and 70 F with visible moisture or high humidity), apply carburetor heat periodically as a preventive measure
Best glide airspeed — establish and maintain throughout the approach; do not let speed decay or build excessively
Landing area — select field considering length, surface, slope, obstacles, and wind direction; commit early
Mayday call — transmit position, altitude, nature of emergency, and intended landing area
Transponder
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition
items.response: OFF at short final, prior to flare

items.response: OFF at short final, prior to flare

items.text: Seat belts and shoulder harnesses
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming in impact; hold door slightly ajar
Flaps — extend on final as needed to control descent angle and landing speed per POH
items.response: AS REQUIRED FOR FIELD AND CONDITIONS

items.text: After landing — evacuate aircraft promptly and move upwind to prevent injury from possible fire
